You are part of an optimization system that improves a given text (i.e. the variable). You are the gradient (feedback) engine. Your only responsibility is to give intelligent and creative feedback and constructive criticism to variables, given an objective specified in <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> </OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> tags. The variables may be solutions to problems, prompts to language models, code, or any other text-based variable. Pay attention to the role description of the variable, and the context in which it is used. You should assume that the variable will be used in a similar context in the future. Only provide strategies, explanations, and methods to change in the variable. DO NOT propose a new version of the variable, that will be the job of the optimizer. Your only job is to send feedback and criticism (compute 'gradients'). For instance, feedback can be in the form of 'Since language models have the X failure mode...', 'Adding X can fix this error because...', 'Removing X can improve the objective function because...', 'Changing X to Y would fix the mistake ...', that gets at the downstream objective.
If a variable is already working well (e.g. the objective function is perfect, an evaluation shows the response is accurate), you should not give feedback.

# - <LM_INPUT>: The input to the language model.
# - <LM_OUTPUT>: The output of the language model.
# - <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION>: The objective of the optimization task.
# - <VARIABLE>: Specifies the span of the variable.
# - <ROLE>: The role description of the variable.
payload.instruction: Change the background into a basketball court
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: Does the image show the background changed into a recognizable basketball court?
node.criteria: Judge only the requested background change, using both supports and the original image as context. Complete (yes) if the background is visibly a basketball court, supported by a recognizable playing surface and court markings or basketball equipment. Partial if some requested progress is visible but the background is not yet recognizably a basketball court; either support may provide evidence of such progress, but neither alone guarantees it. Absent (no) if there is no visible progress toward a basketball-court background. Unknown if the evidence is insufficient to determine whether any requested progress occurred; required unknown evidence remains unresolved. Unrelated edits do not count as progress.
node.binding: Target: The background is visibly a basketball court, with recognizable court features such as a playing surface and court markings or basketball equipment.. Reference: The input image and the requested background change in R1..

node_traces.evidence: The edited background is reported to show a basketball hoop and net, basketballs, and court markings, making it recognizable as a basketball court. Although one support notes a plain, featureless surface, the other provides evidence of recognizable court features; together the saved observations support completion of the requested background change.

dependencies.evidence: The background shows a basketball hoop and balls, but the visible surface is a plain, featureless dark area rather than a recognizable basketball playing surface.
The edited background visibly includes a basketball hoop and net, basketballs, and court markings, which are recognizable basketball-court elements.

response.content: {"text":"The binding is too vague and the aggregate incorrectly treats conflicting support as cumulative proof: the edited image shows a hoop, balls, and a court line, but the large dark background is not clearly a recognizable playing surface. Preserve the distinction between complete and partial progress: equipment alone can establish progress, not completion when the surface/court context is absent or ambiguous. Reconcile the supports against the image and original request rather than letting one positive support override the other; explicitly assess whether the background itself reads as a court. Keep uncertainty available when evidence cannot resolve that criterion. This is a semantic evidence/aggregation issue, not a transport or schema failure."}
